report.summary: Reviewed daedalus/kairos/drafts.py chunk 1/2: persisted advisory drafts with save/list/get/delete functions, path-safe ID validation, and docstring claims about FrugalGPT loop, safety model, and CLI/webapp integration.
risks: _safe_path | medium | Symlink escape not fully prevented: resolve() may follow symlinks outside DRAFT_DIR if a symlink inside points out; the relative_to check blocks traversal but symlinks could still point outside. | Add symlink resolution: check p.resolve().parent == DRAFT_DIR.resolve() or use strict=True in resolve() (Python 3.6+).

_safe_path | low | _ID_RE allows '.' and '_' which are safe for filenames but could be confused with hidden files or extensions; no actual risk given the .json suffix. | No action needed unless security audit demands stricter pattern.

delete_draft | low | Deletes only if _safe_path returns non-None and file exists; no check that the file is actually a draft (not a symlink to something else). | Add is_file() check (already present) and optionally verify JSON content before deletion.
list_drafts | low | Ignores JSON decode errors silently; could hide corrupted drafts. | Log or report decode errors for debugging.

save_draft | low | Never overwrites, but if many drafts in same second, filename collision loop increments n indefinitely; unlikely but possible. | Add a max iteration limit or use microsecond timestamp.

claims.text: An advisory-mode task legitimately writes nothing: the free lane produces a PROPOSAL that a write-capable, trusted lane (Claude / the user) applies later.
claims.why: This claim describes the design rationale behind advisory mode; no code in this chunk implements or verifies that behavior.

claims.text: Until now that proposal lived only inside the offload result and evaporated when the caller dropped it.
claims.why: Refers to prior behavior not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Here every accepted advisory report is persisted to runs/drafts/<ts>-<slug>.json
claims.why: save_draft writes to DRAFT_DIR which is ROOT / 'runs' / 'drafts', and filename is timestamp-slug with .json extension.

claims.text: so it can be listed, reviewed, applied, and cleaned up later -- daedalus drafts list|show|rm.
claims.why: CLI commands not present in this chunk; list_drafts, get_draft, delete_draft provide the corresponding functionality.

claims.text: Apply is deliberately NOT automated: a draft is a proposal, and the safety model says a free model may propose but never merge.
claims.why: No code in this chunk enforces that apply is not automated; it's a design statement.

claims.text: Applying stays a human / Claude action (Era-3 follow-up wires it into the webapp queue view).
claims.why: Refers to future integration not present in this chunk.

claims.text: A draft id is our own timestamp-slug stem. It arrives from the CLI and from URL path segments (/api/drafts/<id>/apply), so it MUST NOT be trusted into a filesystem path -- reject anything that isn't a plain stem (no separators, no traversal). Closes the path-traversal gap Minos would have flagged.
claims.why: _ID_RE pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,120}$ rejects separators, traversal, and ensures alphanumeric with limited special chars; _safe_path uses it and resolves to ensure the path stays inside DRAFT_DIR.

claims.text: Resolve a draft id to its file ONLY if the id is a plain stem that stays inside DRAFT_DIR. Returns None for anything suspicious (.., separators, absolute paths, symlink escapes).
claims.why: Function checks _ID_RE match, constructs path, resolves and verifies relative_to DRAFT_DIR, returns None on failure. Symlink escape is partially addressed: resolve() follows symlinks, but relative_to checks the resolved path; a symlink inside DRAFT_DIR pointing outside would still be blocked because the resolved path would not be relative to DRAFT_DIR.

observations.what: DRAFT_DIR is derived from __file__ parents[2], which assumes the module is at daedalus/kairos/drafts.py; this is fragile if the package structure changes.

_safe_path uses resolve() which follows symlinks; a symlink inside DRAFT_DIR pointing outside could pass the relative_to check if the symlink target is outside but the resolved path is still inside? Actually resolve() returns the real path, so if a symlink inside points to /etc, resolved path is /etc, which is not relative to DRAFT_DIR, so it's rejected. So it's safe.
save_draft does not validate the report dict structure; it just stores whatever is passed.
list_drafts reads all .json files in DRAFT_DIR; if a non-draft file is present, it will try to parse it and skip on error.
delete_draft returns False for invalid IDs or missing files; no error is raised.
